turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Collectors often talk about a daily beater and a safe queen. What do those terms mean?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A daily beater is a watch you wear every day without worrying. You wear it to work, to the gym, maybe even while gardening. If it gets a scratch, that's fine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's a watch that spends most of its life in a safe or a box. It's usually expensive, rare or very important to its owner. It only comes out for special occasions.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It sounds a little sad for the watch.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A lot of people feel that way. A watch is made to be worn. If you never wear it, you lose the joy of having it on your wrist.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: But I understand the fear. If a watch is very valuable, every scratch hurts.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Exactly. That's the collector mindset. You're always balancing two things: enjoying the watch now, and protecting its condition and value for the future.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I try to wear everything at least sometimes. I also remind myself that small marks tell a story. Years later, a scratch can remind you of a trip or a special day. A perfect watch in a safe doesn't have any stories.
